items.name: Berserker
items.description: Fast light melee infantry, dual axes, high damage. Berserkergang: at low health, heals and deals bonus damage for a time. Dark Age availability is fandom infobox only. Fandom S&W: strong vs light units, weak vs archers.

videoSources.note: Starting Villager Capacity: the Villager counter reads 6/10 at game time 00:02, before any Longhouse exists. Each Longhouse adds +10. The Overview reads 'The Villager Capacity is increased by +10 for each Longhouse constructed.' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00012.jpg). The Longhouse tooltip reads 'Increases your Villager capacity by +10 and your maximum Population by +25.' (ehO1BOe7wG8/s_00174.jpg). The HUD then goes 6/10 -> 10/20 -> 16/30 (nd74LibluQ0 1:38, 5:25, 7:10). The highest capacity seen in any recording is 200 (e.g. nd74LibluQ0 41:40, 72/200). That is not proven to be a hard maximum.

items.name: Imperial population
items.description: After reaching Imperial Age the Vikings can increase maximum population to 210 regardless of landmark; Folkekirken (via Kongens Dør Cathedral) raises it to 220.

fields.value: Both Age IV landmarks increase population and maximum population by +10, so max population goes from 200 to 210. Kongens Dør Cathedral (Age IV Economic Landmark) acts as a Monastery and has a unique technology (Folkekirken) that adds another +10, for 220. Rikets Nyckel Castle (Age IV Defensive Landmark) gives +10 only (210).

videoSources.quote: Kongens Dør Cathedral Age IV - Economic Landmark 2400 1200 4m 10s Acts as a Monastery. Increases population and maximum population by +10. Has a slowly expanding area that gathers a tithe of 10 Gold for each Longhouse every 30 seconds. Has a unique technology that further increases maximum population. | Rikets Nyckel Castle Age IV - Defensive Landmark 2400 1200 4m 10s Acts as a Keep that fires volleys of arrows. Increases population and maximum population by +10. Reduces the cost of all unit tier technologies by 50%. Recruits 10 Skåne Crossbowmen upon construction completion.
videoSources.value: Both Age IV landmarks increase population and maximum population by +10, so max population goes from 200 to 210. Rikets Nyckel Castle (Age IV Defensive Landmark) gives +10 only (210).

items.name: Late-game roster shift
items.description: As the civilization develops it gains access to Knights (Jylland Knights, Castle Age) and 'Militia Crossbowmen' (fandom: Skâne Crossbowman).

fields.value: In Castle Age (III) the Vikings get two cheaper, weaker variants of standard units. The Stable gets the Jylland Knight (Heavy Melee Cavalry, 120 food 90 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health', grants 10 Gold on death). The Archery Range gets Skåne Crossbowmen (Light Ranged Infantry, 75 food 30 gold, 'Lower cost but with reduced damage and health'). Both read 'Requirements: Castle Age (III)'.

videoSources.quote: JYLLAND KNIGHT Heavy Melee Cavalry 120 90 Unique to Vikings Expensive cavalry with high damage and melee armor. Effective against melee units. Lower cost but with reduced damage and health. + Heavy armor + Strong in melee combat + Grants 10 Gold on death - Countered by Spearmen and Crossbowmen Requirements: Castle Age (III)
videoSources.value: In Castle Age (III) the Vikings get two cheaper, weaker variants of standard units. videoSources.transcribedBy: opus-agent gap hunt vik-attachments + blind re-read
videoSources.note: Seconds per gold tick. The camera is static from game 19:01 to 19:17. At 10 fps the '+8' popup first appears at video 975.6, 985.9 and 996.1, so about 10.2-10.3 game seconds apart (game clock runs 1:1 with video there). The hovered timer reads 10 at 15:58 and 9 at 15:59; the 10 is in a sub-second re-extract at scratchpad nd/f_832.6.jpg. So the timer is 10 s, not 9.6. 8 gold per 10 s is 48 gold/min, against the tooltip's 'Generates 50 Gold per minute'.
